relevance_reason: This is a population biobank study. Its only LRRK2 content is a description of individuals carrying homozygous LRRK2 loss-of-function variants. These people had reduced kidney function, and none is described as having Parkinson disease. That gives context on the PARK8 gene's mechanism (risk comes from gain of function) and on the safety of LRRK2 inhibitors, but it does not describe PARK8 patients.

findings.statement: Koch et al. (2026) noted that gain of function of LRRK2 increases Parkinson disease risk. They stated that heterozygous predicted loss-of-function (pLoF) variants of LRRK2 have not been associated with any phenotype, including Parkinson disease. They reported this while assessing the safety of chronic LRRK2 inhibition in the Pakistan Genome Resource (173,303 exomes and genomes).
quotes: LRRK2 is a broadly expressed protein kinase gene in which gain of function increases Parkinson’s disease risk.
Heterozygous pLoF of LRRK2 has not been associated with any phenotypes, including Parkinson’s disease.

findings.statement: In the Pakistan Genome Resource, Koch et al. (2026) found a 42-year-old individual homozygous for an LRRK2 splice donor variant (c.706+1G>T). This person had a low eGFR of 68 ml/min, consistent with early-stage kidney disease. In this person's exome, the authors found no damaging missense or high-confidence pLoF variants in known kidney disease genes.
quotes: (1) a 42-year-old individual with a homozygous splice donor variant (Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) coding sequence c.706+1G>T) and low eGFR of 68 ml min−1, consistent with early-stage kidney disease

In the two PGR homLoF variant carriers for which exomes were available, we evaluated variants (with MAF < 1%) in known kidney disease genes (PKD1, PKD2, COL4A3, COL4A4, COL4A5, HNF1B, UMOD or APOL1) and found no damaging missense (REVEL score > 0.7) or high-confidence pLoF variants.

findings.statement: Koch et al. (2026) found a 25-year-old individual in the Pakistan Genome Resource homozygous for an LRRK2 frameshift variant (Arg1639GlyfsTer15). This person had chronic kidney disease, with an eGFR of 14 ml/min.
quotes: (2) a 25-year-old individual with chronic kidney disease (eGFR = 14 ml min−1) who was homozygous for a frameshift (Arg1639GlyfsTer15)

findings.statement: In a recall-by-genotype study, Koch et al. (2026) identified a 49-year-old woman homozygous for an LRRK2 splice donor variant (c.1418+1G>T), confirmed by Sanger sequencing. She was the only homozygous carrier in her family. Her eGFR was 51 ml/min, suggestive of kidney disease, and lower than that of all 13 recruited relatives: 6 heterozygous carriers and 7 non-carriers.
quotes: RBG of LRRK2 pLoF variant carriers and their consenting family members identified a 49-year-old female individual who was homozygous for a LRRK2 splice donor variant, c.1418+1G>T (Extended Data Fig. 11a).

This individual was the sole carrier of a homLoF variant identified in her family and had an eGFR of 51 ml min−1, suggestive of kidney disease. Her eGFR was lower than all 13 of her recruited heterozygous and non-carrier family members

phenotypes.text: reduced eGFR suggestive of kidney disease

findings.statement: Koch et al. (2026) said their sample of human LRRK2 homozygous loss-of-function carriers was small. They concluded that the kidney dysfunction seen in these carriers supports the adverse renal phenotypes reported in LRRK2-knockout rodents and in preclinical studies of LRRK2 inhibitors in rats and non-human primates. They suggested that kidney function be monitored during long-term LRRK2 inhibition.
quotes: the observation of kidney dysfunction in these individuals provides human data that support the adverse renal phenotypes observed in LRRK2-knockout rodent models– and the preclinical renal findings of LRRK2 inhibitors in rats and non-human primates. Kidney function should be monitored during long-term LRRK2 inhibition.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It appears to be an editorial or commentary on whether the link between Parkinson disease, cancer, and LRRK2 is causal or only an association. It reports no patients, variants, or data.

findings.statement: Bandmann and Cookson (2012) discussed whether the link between LRRK2-associated Parkinson disease and cancer is causal or only an association.
quotes: Parkinson disease, cancer, and LRRK2: causation or association?

relevance_reason: Cross-sectional study of Jewish PD patients showing that LRRK2 G2019S carriers have an increased risk of non-skin cancer, which adds to the PARK8 phenotype (other features).

findings.statement: Inzelberg et al. (2012) genotyped 490 Jewish patients with Parkinson disease for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation and found 79 carriers (16.1%). Non-skin cancer was more common in carriers than in noncarriers (18 of 79 carriers, 23%, vs 49 noncarriers, 12%; p = 0.01, OR 2.18, 95% CI 1.19-3.99). Among Ashkenazi patients, the age-adjusted OR for carriers was 3.38 (95% CI 1.64-6.97, p = 0.0009). The authors concluded that Ashkenazi Jewish patients with PD who carry G2019S are more likely to have a concomitant non-skin cancer than noncarriers.
quotes: Overall, 79/490 (16.1%) genotyped patients carried the G2019S mutation.
Eighteen (23%) carriers vs 49 (12%) noncarriers had a non-skin cancer (p = 0.01, odds ratio [OR] = 2.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.19-3.99).
The OR for LRRK2 mutation carriers adjusted for age was 3.38 (95% CI 1.64-6.97, p = 0.0009).

relevance_reason: Biomarker study of CSF amyloid-beta and tau in symptomatic and asymptomatic LRRK2 mutation carriers, compared with PET measures of dopaminergic function; it adds evidence on PARK8 pathogenesis and biomarkers.

findings.statement: Aasly et al. (2012) measured CSF amyloid beta-42 (Abeta42), total tau, and phosphorylated tau in 26 LRRK2 mutation carriers, 18 asymptomatic and 8 with a phenotype resembling sporadic Parkinson disease. They compared these levels with PET measures of striatal dopaminergic function using 18F-6-fluoro-L-dopa (FD), 11C-dihydrotetrabenazine, and 11C-d-threo-methylphenidate. Lower CSF Abeta42 and tau levels correlated with lower striatal dopaminergic function on all 3 tracers, and the association between Abeta42 and FD uptake was significant. When the analysis was limited to carriers of G2019S, the most common LRRK2 variant in the cohort, the correlations with tau were also significant.
quotes: CSF Aβ42, total tau, and phosphorylated tau were measured with Luminex assays in 26 LRRK2 mutation carriers, who were either asymptomatic (n = 18) or had a phenotype resembling sporadic PD (n = 8).
Reduced CSF Aβ42 and tau levels correlated with lower striatal dopaminergic function as determined by all 3 PET tracers, with a significant association between Aβ42 and FD uptake.
When cases were restricted to carriers of the G2019S mutation, the most common LRRK2 variant in our cohort, significant correlations were also observed for tau.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased amyloid beta 42 peptide CSF concentration

phenotypes.text: reduced striatal dopaminergic function on PET

findings.statement: Aasly et al. (2012) concluded that how amyloid beta and tau are handled is likely important in both LRRK2-related and sporadic Parkinson disease, even in early phases of the disease. They suggested that these CSF proteins might be useful as biomarkers of early or presymptomatic disease.
quotes: The disposition of Aβ and tau is likely important in both LRRK2-related and sporadic PD, even during early phases of the disease.
may provide insights into the pathogenesis of PD and the potential utility of these proteins as biomarkers.

relevance_reason: A family study describing the motor and nonmotor phenotype of people with LRRK2 G2019S-associated Parkinson disease and of mutation carriers without Parkinson disease, compared with idiopathic PD.

findings.statement: Marras et al. (2011) used a family study design to compare 25 individuals with LRRK2 G2019S-associated Parkinson disease with 84 individuals with idiopathic PD, recruited from 4 movement disorders centers. Tremor was more often a presenting feature in LRRK2-PD. LRRK2-PD patients also had better olfactory identification, higher Beck Depression Inventory scores, and worse color discrimination on the Farnsworth-Munsell 100-Hue test. The authors concluded that the phenotype was largely overlapping with idiopathic PD.
quotes: Tremor was more often a presenting feature among 25 individuals with LRRK2-associated PD than among 84 individuals with iPD.

Subjects with LRRK2-PD had better olfactory identification compared with subjects with iPD, higher Beck Depression Inventory scores, and higher error scores on Farnsworth-Munsell 100-Hue test of color discrimination.
Although tremor is a more common presenting feature of LRRK2-PD than iPD and some nonmotor features differed in degree, the phenotype is largely overlapping.

findings.statement: Marras et al. (2011) found that postural or action tremor was more common in 29 nonmanifesting LRRK2 G2019S carriers than in 53 noncarriers from the same families. They suggested that postural or action tremor may be an early sign. Nonparkinsonian family members had higher UPDRS motor scores, more constipation, and worse color discrimination than controls, whether or not they carried the mutation.
quotes: Postural or action tremor was more common among 29 nonmanifesting mutation carriers compared with 53 noncarriers within the families.
Nonparkinsonian family members had higher Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale motor scores, more constipation, and worse color discrimination than controls, regardless of mutation status.
Postural or action tremor may represent an early sign.

relevance_reason: The paper looks at olfactory dysfunction in people who carry the LRRK2 G2019S mutation, both those with Parkinson disease and those without, which adds to the clinical features of PARK8.

findings.statement: Saunders-Pullman et al. (2011) gave the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT) to 31 patients with Parkinson disease related to the LRRK2 G2019S mutation (manifesting carriers), 30 patients with PD who did not carry the mutation, 28 mutation-carrier family members without PD (nonmanifesting carriers), and 46 controls. Compared with controls, mean scores were lower in nonmanifesting carriers (difference = -3.518, p = 0.006), manifesting carriers (difference = -7.677) and noncarrier PD patients (difference = -13.810). Olfaction was better in LRRK2 manifesting carriers than in non-LRRK2 PD patients (difference = 6.13, p = 0.0012). The authors concluded that olfaction is impaired in G2019S-related PD, but less overall than in other PD.
quotes: Compared to controls, the mean score was lower among NMC (difference = -3.518, p = 0.006), MC (difference = -7.677, p < 0.0001), and idiopathic PD (PD-NC) (difference = -13.810, p < 0.0001).
Olfaction was better among MC (PD-MC) than non-LRRK2 PD (PD-NC) (difference = 6.13, p = 0.0012).
Olfaction is impaired in LRRK2 G2019S-mutation related PD, although less overall than other PD.

findings.statement: Saunders-Pullman et al. (2011) found that olfaction was impaired in a subset of 28 nonmanifesting LRRK2 G2019S carriers who did not have PD. The authors suggested that olfaction may be a marker for the development of PD in this group and that longitudinal studies are warranted.
quotes: impaired olfaction was increased overall in LRRK2 carriers both with and without PD, though the impairment was only present in a subset of NMCs.
olfaction is impaired in a subset of LRRK2 NMC, suggesting that olfaction may be a marker for development of PD in this group, and that longitudinal studies are warranted.

relevance_reason: A large cohort study of early-onset PD that reports how often LRRK2 G2019S occurs, how carriers are distributed by ancestry, and their motor phenotype. This adds frequency and phenotype evidence for PARK8.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) screened 953 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (age at onset 50 years or younger) from 13 movement disorders centers in the CORE-PD study. Patients were recruited without regard to family history. Of these, 35 (3.6%) carried the LRRK2 G2019S mutation. Among the 31 G2019S carriers with no mutation in another gene, 30 were heterozygous and 1 was homozygous. One additional patient carried the LRRK2 G2385R variant, and no other pathogenic LRRK2 mutations (R1441C, I2020T, Y1699C) were found.
quotes: One hundred fifty-eight (16.6%) participants had mutations, including 64 (6.7%) PRKN, 35 (3.6%) LRRK2 G2019S, 64 (6.7%) GBA, and 1 (0.2%) DJ1.
Thirty one were LRRK2 G2019S carriers (30 heterozygotes, one homozygote). One subject carried the LRRK2 G2385R variant; no other pathogenic LRRK2 mutations were found.
All samples analyzed by either the MALDI-TOF or the genotyping array were examined for the mutations G2019S, R1441C, I2020T and Y1699C.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) reported that LRRK2 G2019S carriers were more likely to have Jewish ancestry: 55% of G2019S-only carriers were Jewish, compared with 12% of noncarriers. Among patients with Jewish ancestry, 13.6% of those with a family history of PD and 12.2% of those without one carried G2019S. Grandparents' country of origin was known for 11 of the 15 non-Jewish G2019S carriers: 4 reported Southern European descent (Italy or Portugal), 4 mixed European descent, 1 Eastern European ancestry, and 2 Puerto Rican ancestry.
quotes: The association was driven by LRRK2 G2019S carriers and GBA N370S carriers who were more likely to be Jewish than non-Jewish (Table 4).

Of the 15 G2019S carriers who did not report Jewish ancestry, data on grandparents' country of origin was available on 11. Four reported Southern European decent (Italy or Portugal) and 4 reported mixed European decent
One reported Eastern European ancestry (Russia and Latvia) and two carriers reported Puerto-Rican ancestry.
findings.population: Jewish; Southern European; mixed European; Puerto Rican

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that LRRK2 G2019S carriers with early-onset PD were more likely to have the postural instability and gait difficulty (PIGD) motor phenotype than noncarriers: 96% (25 carriers) versus 58% of noncarriers. Carriers had a mean age at onset of 42 years, similar to noncarriers. The presenting symptom did not differ significantly between mutation groups.
quotes: LRRK2 G2019S carriers were more likely to manifest the PIGD motor phenotype, and GBA L444P carriers had higher scores on the UPDRS-III
There was no significant difference in the presenting symptom of PD among the groups; 44% presented with rest tremor,13% with stiffness and 7% with action tremor.

phenotypes.text: postural instability and gait difficulty motor phenotype

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that PRKN carriers were more likely than LRRK2 carriers to report a family history of PD, even though LRRK2-related PD is autosomal dominant. Among G2019S carriers, 3.6% of patients with a family history of PD carried the mutation, compared with 3.1% of those without one. The authors suggested that one explanation was incomplete penetrance of G2019S. They also noted that the penetrance of these mutations remains unknown.
quotes: PRKN carriers were more likely to report a FHPD than LRRK2 carriers, despite the fact that LRRK2 is autosomal dominant and PRKN is considered a recessive disorder.

This finding could be explained by siblings of PRKN carriers who may develop PD at a younger age than siblings of other mutation carriers (i.e. LRRK2 siblings may develop the disease at a later age) and by incomplete penetrance of the G2019S mutation.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) identified 4 patients who carried LRRK2 G2019S together with a mutation in another gene. One Jewish man carried a heterozygous PRKN exon 5-6 deletion (onset at age 41). One non-Jewish man carried GBA L444P (onset at age 31). Two Jewish patients carried GBA N370S (onset at ages 47 and 49). None of these patients reported PD in a first-degree relative.
quotes: 1. | LRRK2 G2019S PRKN exon 5–6 deletion heterozygote | Male | yes | 41 | 51 | 10 | NA | 900 | 30 | None
Demographic and disease characteristics of seven individuals who carried more than one mutation are described in Table 2. None of these subjects reported a FHPD in a first-degree relative.

relevance_reason: Functional and animal-model study showing that LRRK2 G2019S neurotoxicity is kinase dependent and can be blocked pharmacologically, bearing on PARK8 pathogenesis, animal models, and potential treatment.

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) screened 84 kinase and phosphatase inhibitors at 16 microM against LRRK2 autophosphorylation and LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of myelin basic protein, and identified 8 compounds, including indolinone compounds (staurosporine, GF 109203X, Ro 31-8220, 5-iodotubercidin, GW5074, indirubin-3-prime-monooxime) and anthracene compounds (SP 600125, damnacanthal), that substantially inhibited LRRK2 kinase activity; none of the inhibitors enhanced LRRK2 kinase activity.
quotes: LRRK2 autophosphorylation (Fig. 1) and LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of myelin basic protein (MBP) (Supplementary Fig. 1) were monitored in the presence or absence of 84 Biomol kinase and phosphatase inhibitors at 16 μM

Indolinone compounds including staurosporine (compound 6), GF 109203X (compound 31), Ro 31- 8220 (compound 33), 5-iodotubercidin (compound 49), GW5074 (compound 56), and indirubin-3′-monooxime (compound 70) and anthracene compounds, SP 600125 (compound 68), damnacanthal (compound 22) substantially inhibit LRRK2 autophosphorylation
None of the inhibitors significantly enhanced LRRK2 kinase activity.

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) determined IC50 values of the 8 inhibitors against autophosphorylation and MBP phosphorylation by wildtype and G2019S LRRK2, and found that all inhibitors except indirubin-3-prime-monooxime had relatively similar potency against wildtype and G2019S LRRK2 autophosphorylation; indirubin-3-prime-monooxime more potently inhibited LRRK2 G2019S autophosphorylation. All 8 inhibitors had a similar inhibitory profile against LRRK1.
quotes: The IC50’s of the 8 inhibitors were determined against autophosphorylation and MBP phosphorylation by wild type (WT) and G2019S LRRK2

All the inhibitors except indirubin-3′-monooxime have relatively similar potency against WT and G2019S LRRK2 autophosphoryation activity (Fig. 1c, d and Supplementary Table 2). Indirubin-3′-monooxime more potently inhibits LRRK2 G2019S autophosphorylation.
All 8 inhibitors have a similar inhibitory profile against LRRK1 autophosphorylation and MBP phosphorylation (Supplementary Fig. 2a d).

findings.statement: Because LRRK2 and LRRK1 are related to the MAP kinase kinase kinase Raf, Lee et al. (2010) tested additional Raf kinase inhibitors and concluded that GW5074 inhibited both LRRK2 and LRRK1 kinase activities, that sorafenib and Raf inhibitor IV were relatively selective for LRRK2 kinase activity, and that ZM336372 had minimal to no effect on either kinase. GW5074 and indirubin-3-prime-monooxime, but not ZM336372 or indirubin, also inhibited LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of 4E-BP1, a putative physiologic LRRK2 substrate.
quotes: These results taken together indicate that GW5074 inhibits both LRRK2 and LRRK1 kinase activities, whereas Sorafenib and Raf inhibitor IV are relatively selective for LRRK2 kinase activity and ZM336372 has minimal to no effect on both LRRK2 and LRRK1 kinase activities.

GW5074 and indirubin-3′-monooxime also inhibit LRRK2-mediated eukaryotic initiation factor 4E (eIF4E)-binding protein (4E-BP1), a putative physiologic LRRK2 substrate, whereas ZM336372 and indirubin do not inhibit LRRK2 phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 (Fig. 1h, i).

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) found that overexpression of both wildtype and G2019S LRRK2 led to primary cortical neuron injury assessed by neurite shortening, and that LRRK2 G2019S overexpression also led to cell death assessed by TUNEL, whereas kinase-dead versions of LRRK2 wildtype (D1994A) and LRRK2 G2019S (G2019S, D1994A) were devoid of toxicity.
quotes: Both LRRK2 WT and LRRK2 G2019S overexpression leads to primary cortical neuron injury as assessed by neurite shortening (Fig. 2a, b and Supplementary Fig. 3) and LRRK2 G2019S overexpression leads to cell death as assessed by DNA fragmentation (TdT-mediated X-dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) assay)
whereas a kinase dead versions of LRRK2 WT (D1994A) and LRRK2 G2019S (G2019S, D1994) are devoid of toxicity as previously described

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) showed that treatment of cortical cultures with GW5074, indirubin-3-prime-monooxime, or the relatively LRRK2-selective inhibitor sorafenib (each 0.5 microM) attenuated or completely prevented LRRK2 G2019S cell injury and cell death, whereas ZM336372 and indirubin, which do not inhibit LRRK2 or LRRK1 kinase activity, failed to protect; the authors concluded that the protection was due to inhibition of LRRK2 kinase activity rather than inhibition of Raf, cyclin-dependent kinase, or GSK3-beta.
quotes: Treatment of the cortical cultures with 0.5 μM GW5074 and 0.5 μM indirubin-3′-monooxime, which inhibit both LRRK2 and LRRK1, attenuate LRRK2 G2019S cell injury and cell death (Fig. 2b, d).
The Raf kinase inhibitor, ZM336372 (0.5 μM), which does not inhibit either LRRK2 or LRRK1 kinase activity fails to inhibit LRRK2 G2019S toxicity

These results taken together indicate that the protection afforded by the Raf inhibitors (GW5074 and Sorafenib) and the cyclin-dependent kinase and GSK-3β inhibitor, indirubin-3′-monooxime, are due to inhibition of LRRK2 kinase activity

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) developed a herpes simplex virus amplicon-based mouse model of LRRK2 dopaminergic neurotoxicity. HSV amplicon-mediated delivery of LRRK2 G2019S induced significant loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive substantia nigra neurons 3 weeks after stereotaxic injection into the ipsilateral striatum compared with LRRK2 wildtype and eGFP control viruses, whereas the kinase-dead LRRK2 G2019S, D1994A caused no neuronal loss, despite equivalent levels of overexpression.
quotes: To determine the efficacy of the LRRK2 kinase inhibitors in vivo, a herpes simplex virus (HSV) amplicon-based mouse model of LRRK2 DA neurotoxicity was developed

HSV amplicon-mediated delivery of LRRK2 G2019S induces significant loss of TH-positive neurons 3 weeks after stereotaxic injection into the ipsilateral striatum of mice compared to LRRK2 WT and eGFP control viruses (Fig. 2f, g). HSV amplicon-mediated delivery of LRRK2 G2019S, D1994A causes no neuronal loss similar to LRRK2 WT and GFP control viruses
Immunoblot analysis confirms that WT, G2019S and G2019S, D1994A LRRK2 are overexpressed at equivalent levels (Fig. 2e).

phenotypes.text: loss of dopaminergic substantia nigra neurons

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) reported that twice daily intraperitoneal injections of the LRRK2 kinase inhibitors GW5074 and indirubin-3-prime-monooxime (2.5 mg/kg) attenuated the loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons induced by HSV-LRRK2 G2019S in mice compared with DMSO- and indirubin-injected controls, and that GW5074 also rescued the reduced density of TH-positive fibers and prevented the increase in isolectin B4-positive inflammatory cells in the striatum and substantia nigra compacta.
quotes: Twice daily injections of the LRRK2 kinase inhibitors, GW5074 and indirubin-3′-monooxime, (2.5 mg/kg, i.p.) attenuate the loss of TH-positive neurons induced by HSV-LRRK2 G2019S/CMVeGFP compared to DMSO and indirubin injected controls (Fig. 2f, h).
the reduction in the density of TH-positive fibers is rescued by GW5074 (Supplementary Fig. 5)
but LRRK2 G2019S induces a significant increase of ILB4-positive cells in the striatum and SNc, which is also prevented by administration of GW5074 (Supplementary Fig. 6)

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) concluded that their identification of kinase inhibitors that inhibit LRRK2 kinase activity and protect against LRRK2 toxicity in vitro and in vivo established that LRRK2-induced degeneration of neurons in vivo is kinase dependent and that pharmacologic LRRK2 kinase inhibition is a potentially promising neuroprotective therapeutic modality for Parkinson disease; they cautioned, however, that an authentic LRRK2 substrate has yet to be identified, raising concerns about the physiologic relevance of screens based on autophosphorylation and artificial substrates.
quotes: These results establish that LRRK2-induced degeneration of neurons in vivo is kinase dependent and that LRRK2 kinase inhibition provides a potential new neuroprotective paradigm for the treatment of Parkinson's disease.

Since an authentic substrate of LRRK2 has yet to be identified, there should be a note of caution regarding the physiological relevance of the screens used in this and related studies based on autophosphorylation and artificial substrates.
they demonstrate that pharmacologic inhibition of LRRK2 kinase activity is a potentially promising therapeutic modality for the treatment of neurodegeneration in PD

findings.statement: Lee et al. (2010) noted that LRRK2 mutations are a common cause of Parkinson disease, that patients with LRRK2 mutations are clinically and neurochemically indistinguishable from those with idiopathic Parkinson disease, and that disease-segregating LRRK2 mutations lead to neurotoxicity in vitro and loss of dopamine neurons in patients with Parkinson disease.
quotes: Leucine-rich repeat kinase-2 (LRRK2) mutations are a common cause of Parkinson's disease.

Patients with LRRK2 mutations are clinically and neurochemically indistinguishable from idiopathic PD. Disease segregating mutations in LRRK2 lead to neurotoxicity in vitro – and loss of dopamine neurons in PD patients.

phenotypes.text: parkinsonism indistinguishable from idiopathic Parkinson disease

relevance_reason: Case-control association study in Chinese subjects, plus a meta-analysis with Japanese cohorts, showing that SNPs at the PARK8 locus are associated with increased PD risk in Asians.

findings.statement: Tan et al. (2010) analyzed 13 SNPs at Parkinson disease GWAS-linked loci (PARK16, PARK8, PARK1, and BST1) in 2 case-control cohorts totaling 1,349 ethnic Chinese subjects. PARK8 SNPs were associated with an increased risk of PD. A pooled analysis with 2 Japanese replication cohorts, involving 1,366 PD patients and 16,669 controls, showed robust association with the PARK8 locus. The authors concluded that the strength of association was similar in Chinese and Japanese subjects.
quotes: We conducted an analysis of 13 SNPs associated with PD GWAS-linked loci in 2 case-control cohorts comprised of 1,349 ethnic Chinese subjects.
PARK16 SNPs were associated with a decreased risk while PARK1 and PARK8 SNPs were associated with an increased risk of PD.
A pooled analysis of our Chinese cohorts and 2 Japanese replication cohorts involving 1,366 subjects with PD and 16,669 controls revealed robust association with these 3 loci and also BST1.

relevance_reason: Functional and Drosophila model study of pathogenic LRRK2 mutations (G2019S, I2020T, R1441G; fly I1915T) elucidating a disease mechanism for PARK8; no human patients described.

findings.statement: Using an in vivo EGFP reporter carrying let-7-binding sites in its 3'UTR, Gehrke et al. (2010) showed that ubiquitous (Da-Gal4) or dopaminergic neuron-specific (TH-Gal4) expression of pathogenic Drosophila dLRRK(I1915T) or human LRRK2(G2019S) stimulated reporter expression more than the wild-type proteins, whereas dLRRK RNAi decreased reporter expression and the kinase-dead dLRRK(3KD) had no effect; gfp mRNA levels were unchanged, leading the authors to conclude that LRRK2 antagonizes let-7 function at the translational level in a kinase-dependent manner.
quotes: Da-Gal4-directed ubiquitous or TH-Gal4-directed DN-specific co-expression of pathogenic dLRRK(I1915T) or hLRRK2(G2019S) all stimulated reporter expression, more so than WT proteins (Fig.1a, 1b).
dLRRK RNAi led to decreased reporter expression, indicating that endogenous dLRRK also impacts miRNA function (Fig.1a). The kinase-dead dLRRK(3KD) did not affect reporter expression (Fig.1a, s1a).

gfp mRNA levels were not affected (Fig.s1b,c). Moreover, the expression of an EGFP transgene without let-7-binding sites in the 3′UTR was not affected by dLRRK(I1915T) (Fig.s3a). LRRK2 thus antagonizes let-7 function at the translational level.

findings.statement: In HEK293T cells transfected with a luciferase reporter bearing let-7-binding sites in the 3'UTR, Gehrke et al. (2010) found that hLRRK2(I2020T) or hLRRK2(G2019S) efficiently suppressed the inhibitory effect of let-7 on reporter expression, and that introduction of kinase-inactivating (3KD) mutations into these proteins abolished the effect, supporting kinase activity-dependency of pathogenic LRRK2 action.
quotes: hLRRK2(I2020T) or hLRRK2(G2019S) efficiently suppressed the inhibitory effect of let-7 on reporter expression (Fig.s2a,s2b). Introduction of kinase-inactivating mutations (3KD) into hLRRK2-G2019S or -I2020T abolished the effects of these proteins on reporter expression (Fig.s2b), supporting kinase activity-dependency of pathogenic LRRK2 action.

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) reported that mutant hLRRK2 carrying the pathogenic R1441G mutation had no effect on let-7 miRNA function and that transgenic flies expressing dLRRK carrying the equivalent R1069G mutation showed no dopaminergic neuron loss, suggesting that this mutation acts through a different mechanism from G2019S and I2020T.
quotes: Mutant hLRRK2 carrying another pathogenic mutation R1441G had no effect on let-7 miRNA function (Fig.s2b), and transgenic flies expressing dLRRK carrying the equivalent R1069G mutation showed no DN loss (Fig.s2c), suggesting that this mutation act through a different mechanism.

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) showed by co-immunoprecipitation that LRRK2 physically associates with Argonaute proteins of the RNA-induced silencing complex: transfected hLRRK2 associated with hAgo2 in HEK293T cells, transgenic hLRRK2 associated with dAgo1 in fly head extracts, and endogenous hLRRK2 or dLRRK associated with hAgo2 or dAgo1, respectively; because similar results were obtained with or without RNase A treatment, the authors concluded the interaction was likely direct and not RNA-mediated. let-7 levels were not changed in hLRRK2(G2019S) or dLRRK(I1915T) transgenics.
quotes: In co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays, transfected hLRRK2 associated with hAgo2 in HEK293T cells (Fig.1c), transgenic hLRRK2 associated with dAgo1 in fly head extracts (Fig.1f), and endogenous hLRRK2 or dLRRK associated with hAgo2 or dAgo1, respectively (Fig.1d, 1e, s6b).
Since similar co-IP results were obtained with (Fig.1c,f) or without (Fig.s6a,c) RNase A treatment of extracts, the interaction was likely direct and not mediated by RNA.
No significant change of let-7 level in hLRRK2(G2019S) or dLRRK(I1915T) transgenics was detected (Fig.s4a).

findings.statement: In Drosophila, Gehrke et al. (2010) found that dAgo1 protein was significantly reduced by pathogenic hLRRK2 in aged flies (but not young flies) and increased in dLRRK mutants, and that ago1 heterozygosity exacerbated the climbing defect and dopaminergic neuron loss phenotypes of pathogenic dLRRK or hLRRK2 transgenics, while aged ago1 heterozygotes alone (with ~26% reduction of dAgo1) showed no obvious phenotype.
quotes: While no significant change in dAgo1 level was observed in young flies (Fig.s7a), in aged flies dAgo1 protein was significantly reduced by pathogenic hLRRK2 (Fig.1g, s5b). Conversely, dAgo1 level was increased in dLRRK mutant (Fig.1g, s7a).

Consistent with a negative regulation of dAgo1 by LRRK2, ago1 heterozygosity exacerbated the climbing defect (Fig.s8b) and DN loss phenotypes (Fig.1i) in pathogenic dLRRK or hLRRK2 transgenics. Aged ago1 heterozygote showed ~26% reduction of dAgo1 protein compared to control and did not exhibit obvious phenotypes

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) demonstrated a genetic interaction between LRRK2 and the miRNA-processing enzyme Dicer in Drosophila: in a TH-Gal4>dLRRK(I1915T) background, Dicer1 overexpression suppressed and Dicer1 RNAi exacerbated dLRRK(I1915T) toxicity, whereas stronger Dicer1 inhibition in a dicer1 heterozygous background itself caused dopaminergic neuron loss and climbing defects that were partially reduced by dLRRK RNAi.
quotes: In TH-Gal4>dLRRK(I1915T) background, Dicer1 overexpression suppressed, whereas Dicer1 RNAi exacerbated, dLRRK(I1915T) toxicity, although similar manipulations in a wild type background had no obvious effect (Fig.1h, s8a).

However, stronger inhibition of Dicer1 by Dicer1 RNAi in dicer1 heterozygous background did result in DN loss and climbing defects (Fig.1j, s8c), which were partially reduced by dLRRK RNAi (Fig.s8d, s19a).

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) found that 4E-BP1 associated with hAgo2 in HEK293T cells and that dLRRK(I1915T) and hLRRK2(G2019S) promoted this interaction more effectively than wild-type proteins, presumably through increased phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 and preferential binding of phospho-4E-BP1 to hAgo2; phospho-mimetic 4E-BP(TE) attenuated let-7 effects and was toxic to dopaminergic neurons, whereas non-phosphorylatable 4E-BP(TA) blocked the ability of hLRRK2(G2019S) to antagonize let-7. The authors concluded that pathogenic hLRRK2 with hyperactive kinase activity promotes association of phospho-4E-BP with hAgo2, relieving miRNA-mediated translational repression.
quotes: 4E-BP1 associated with hAgo2 in HEK293T cells (Fig.s10a). dLRRK(I1915T) and hLRRK2(G2019S) more effectively promoted this interaction than WT proteins. This presumably resulted from increased phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 by pathogenic LRRK2, and preferential binding of phospho-4E-BP1 to hAgo2 (Fig.s10b, s10c).

Pathogenic hLRRK2 with hyperactive kinase activity thus promotes the association of phospho-4E-BP with hAgo2, relieving miRNA-mediated translational repression. Consistently, non-phosphorylatable 4E-BP(TA) blocked the effect of hLRRK2(G2019S) in antagonizing let-7 (Fig.s10j).

findings.statement: By mRNA translational profiling of Da-Gal4>dLRRK(WT) versus Da-Gal4>dLRRK(I1915T) fly heads, Gehrke et al. (2010) identified e2f1 and dp as targets whose translation is upregulated by pathogenic LRRK2; E2F1 and DP protein were increased by dLRRK(I1915T) or hLRRK2(G2019S) and decreased in dLRRK(-/-) mutants without changes in mRNA level, and removing one copy of e2f1 or dp, or overexpressing the negative regulator RBF, suppressed the dopaminergic neuron phenotypes and oxidative stress sensitivity of dLRRK(I1915T) animals, whereas removing one copy of lkb1 had no effect.
quotes: Western blot analysis confirmed upregulation of E2F1 and DP by dLRRK(I1915T) or hLRRK2(G2019S) (Fig.2a, s12a,b); conversely, both proteins were downregulated in dLRRK(−/−) mutant (Fig.2b), with mRNA levels not significantly changed in both conditions (Fig.s12c,d).

Significantly, removing one copy of e2f1 or dp, or overexpressing RBF, a negative regulator of E2F1/DP, suppressed the DN phenotypes in TH-Gal4>dLRRK(I1915T) animals (Fig.2c). Removing one copy of lkb1, another potential target identified by translational profiling, showed no effect (Fig.2c).
Removing one copy of e2f1 or dp, but not lkb1, also attenuated oxidative stress sensitivity of Da-Gal4>dLRRK(I1915T) transgenics (Fig.s13).

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) identified a functional miR-184*-binding site in the Drosophila e2f1 3'UTR and a functional let-7-binding site in the dp 3'UTR by reporter assays, with mutation of two central seed nucleotides abolishing the miRNA effect; co-transfection of pathogenic hLRRK2 strongly relieved the repressive effects of let-7 and miR-184* on the dp- and e2f1-3'UTR reporters, respectively.
quotes: One candidate miR-184*-binding site in e2f1-3′UTR responded to miR-184* activity in reporter assays (Fig.3a). Mutating two central nucleotides in the seed sequence completely abolished this miR-184* effect (Fig.3c, s16a). Similarly, we identified one functional let-7-binding site within dp-3′UTR (Fig.3d, 3f, s16b).
Co-transfection of pathogenic hLRRK2 strongly relieved the repressive effects of let-7 and miR-184* on the expression of dp- or e2f1-3′UTR reporters, respectively (Fig.3b, e).

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) showed that overexpression of pre-let-7 or injection of synthetic let-7 into wild-type fly heads reduced DP protein, and pre-miR-184* or miR-184* injection reduced E2F1, validating E2F1 and DP as in vivo miRNA targets; dopaminergic-neuron-specific pre-let-7 or pre-miR-184* overexpression or mature miRNA injection partially rescued TH-Gal4>dLRRK(I1915T) phenotypes, whereas buffer or control miR-10 injection had no effect, indicating that miRNA regulation of E2F1 and DP is causally involved in dLRRK(I1915T) pathogenesis.
quotes: Ubiquitous overexpression of pre-let-7 (Fig.s4b), or injection of synthetic let-7 (Fig.s3b) significantly reduced DP level in head extracts (Fig. 4a, 4b). Overexpressed pre-miR-184* or injected miR-184* reduced E2F1 level (Fig. 4a, 4b), validating E2F1 and DP as in vivo targets of miR-184* and let-7.

Importantly, DN-specific pre-let-7 or pre-miR-184* overexpression or mature miRNA injection partially rescued TH-Gal4>dLRRK(I1915T) mutant phenotypes, whereas buffer or control miR-10 injection had no effect (Fig. 4a, 4b, s8e).
Regulation of E2F1 and DP by miRNA is therefore causally involved in dLRRK(I1915T) pathogenesis.

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) showed that loss of miRNA function phenocopied pathogenic LRRK2 in Drosophila: homozygous let-7 mutants (Delta-let-7) had reduced locomotor activity, specific reduction of dopaminergic neurons rescuable by a let-7 transgene, and increased DP level, with phenotypes suppressed by removing one copy of dp or e2f1; injection of anti-let-7fS or anti-miR-184*fS antagomirs into wild-type flies increased DP or E2F1 levels and caused specific dopaminergic neuron loss and reduced climbing activity, effects attenuated by e2f1/+ or dp/+ heterozygosity, and E2F1 overexpression alone was sufficient to cause dopaminergic neuron degeneration.
quotes: Homozygous let-7 mutant (Δlet-7) showed reduced locomotor activity and a specific reduction of DNs, which could be rescued by a let-7 transgene (Fig.4c, s8f, s15c, d). Consistent with let-7 regulating DP expression in vivo, DP level was increased in Δlet-7 animals (Fig.4c). Removing one copy of dp or e2f1 suppressed Δlet-7 mutant phenotypes
Anti-let-7fS and anti-miR-184*fS injection resulted in specific DN loss (Fig.4d, s15a, b), and reduced climbing activity (Fig.s9c).

Significantly, the toxic effects of anti-miR-184*fS and anti-let-7fS were attenuated by e2f1/+ or dp/+ heterozygosity (Fig.s9b,c), supporting E2F1/DP as important mediators of antagomir toxicity. Consistently, E2F1 overexpression is sufficient to cause DN degeneration and reduced locomoter activity (Fig.s9f, s15e).

findings.statement: To prove the specificity of the let-7/dp mRNA interaction in dopaminergic neurons, Gehrke et al. (2010) generated flies expressing a dp target protector (dp-TPlet-7), whose ubiquitous expression caused DP overproduction without affecting dp mRNA level and whose TH-Gal4-driven expression led to dopaminergic neuron loss and reduced climbing activity, and genomic dp transgenes with non-functional let-7-binding sites (gDPmut), which caused DP accumulation and, although rescuing viability of Df/dpR217H transheterozygotes, produced loss of dopaminergic neurons and locomotor defects.
quotes: Ubiquitous expression of dp-TPlet-7 using Da-Gal4 resulted in DP overproduction without affecting dp mRNA level (Fig.4e, s18b), and TH-Gal4-driven dp-TPlet-7 expression led to DN loss and reduced climbing activity (Fig.4e, s9d, s19b).

Compared to gDPwt, gDPmut caused DP accumulation in a dp Df/+ background (Fig.4f). Although both gDPwt and gDPmut rescued the viability of Df/dpR217H transheterozygote, gDPmut-rescued animals exhibited loss of DNs and locomotor defects (Fig.4f, s9e, s19c).

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) concluded that gain-of-function LRRK2 mutations cause Parkinson disease by impairing the miRNA pathway: pathogenic LRRK2 antagonizes let-7 and miR-184*, leading to overproduction of E2F1/DP, whose upregulation in post-mitotic neurons may lead to abortive cell division and cell death; because LRRK2 effects manifested only in aged animals, the authors suggested LRRK2 is particularly important for miRNA regulation under stress conditions and proposed novel miRNA-based therapeutic strategies.
quotes: Our results implicate deregulated synthesis of E2F1/DP caused by the miRNA pathway impairment as a key event in LRRK2 pathogenesis and suggest novel miRNA-based therapeutic strategies.
In post-mitotic neurons, their upregulation may lead to abortive cell division and cell death, as shown in DNs of PD patients and animal models.

The fact that the effects of LRRK2 only manifest in aged animals suggests that LRRK2 is particularly important for miRNA regulation under stress conditions, where the function of 4E-BP is also most pronounced.

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) noted that GMR-Gal4-driven dLRRK(I1915T) expression in the eye did not affect the activities of the bantam and miR-14 miRNAs, suggesting that pathogenic dLRRK may regulate miRNA function in a miRNA- and/or tissue-specific manner.
quotes: Interestingly, GMR-Gal4-driven dLRRK(I1915T) expression in the eye did not affect the activities of bantam and miR-14 miRNAs (Fig.s17a, b), which protect against MJD.tr-Q78 and Reaper-induced neurodegeneration, respectively. Thus pathogenic dLRRK may regulate miRNA function in a miRNA- and/or tissue-specific manner.

findings.statement: Gehrke et al. (2010) stated that gain-of-function mutations in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) cause familial as well as sporadic Parkinson disease characterized by age-dependent degeneration of dopaminergic neurons, and that the molecular mechanism of LRRK2 action was not known.
quotes: Gain-of-function mutations in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) cause familial as well as sporadic Parkinson's disease characterized by age-dependent degeneration of dopaminergic neurons. The molecular mechanism of LRRK2 action is not known.

relevance_reason: This is a review abstract on LRRK2 genetics and biology in Parkinson disease. It reports no new patients, variants or experiments and offers only general context.

findings.statement: Dächsel and Farrer (2010) reviewed the molecular genetics and functional biology of LRRK2 in parkinsonism. They noted that genetic mutations that predispose to PD are diagnostically useful in early or atypical presentations. They also noted that affected and asymptomatic LRRK2 carriers provide an opportunity to define the natural history of PD, including penetrance, motor symptoms, nonmotor comorbidities and associated biomarkers.
quotes: Genetic mutations that predispose PD are diagnostically useful in early or atypical presentations.

Both affected and asymptomatic LRRK2 carriers now provide the opportunity to define the natural history of PD. This includes the frequency, penetrance, and rate of motor symptoms, nonmotor comorbidities, and their associated biomarkers.

relevance_reason: Cohort study describing the motor phenotype (PIGD) in early-onset PD patients who carry the LRRK2 G2019S mutation. It adds genotype-phenotype data for PARK8.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2009) genotyped 925 probands with early-onset Parkinson disease (age at onset 50 years or younger) from 13 movement disorders centers for the LRRK2 mutations G2019S, I2020T, R1441C, and Y1699C. Thirty-four probands (3.7%), 14 of whom had been reported before, carried G2019S, and one Ashkenazi Jewish carrier was homozygous. No other mutations were found. Carriers were more likely to be Ashkenazi Jewish than non-carriers (55.9% vs 11.9%) but were not more likely to have a first-degree relative with PD.
quotes: Among 925 probands tested, 34 (3.7%) carried a G2019S mutation. Fourteen (41.2%) of these were previously reported. One carrier, who was AJ, was a G2019S homozygote. None of the other pathogenic mutations (R1441C, Y1699C and I2020T) was found.
Carriers were more likely to report AJ ancestry (55.9% vs. 11.9%, p<0.001), but not more likely to report a first-degree relative with PD than non-carriers.
findings.population: Ashkenazi Jewish and non-Ashkenazi (United States movement disorders centers)

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2009) found that G2019S carriers with early-onset PD had a lower UPDRS tremor score than non-carriers (P = 0.03) and were more likely to have the postural instability and gait difficulty (PIGD) motor phenotype (92.3% vs 58.9%). Only 3.8% of carriers had the tremor-dominant phenotype, compared with 27.4% of non-carriers. The association with PIGD remained after adjustment for disease duration and Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry (OR 17.7) and held in Ashkenazi and non-Ashkenazi probands analyzed separately. The authors found this contrasted with earlier reports linking LRRK2 to tremor-dominant disease.
quotes: Carriers had a lower tremor score (P = .03) and were more likely to have a PIGD phenotype (92.3% vs 58.9%; P = .003). The association of the G2019S mutation with PIGD phenotype remained after controlling for disease duration and Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry (odds ratio, 17.7; P < .001).
After adjustment for disease duration, the association between PIGD and G2019S remained when analyses were performed in 81 AJ and 610 non-AJ separately
Previous reports have suggested that LRRK2 mutations may be associated with tremor in PD.

phenotypes.text: postural instability and gait difficulty phenotype

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2009) found that G2019S carriers and non-carriers with early-onset PD were similar in age at onset (range 13 to 50 years), disease duration, age at examination, UPDRS-III score, MMSE score, and levodopa dose. Among carriers with complete UPDRS data, 88.5% had asymmetric onset and 44.0% presented with rest tremor. Although PIGD was associated with more severe disease than the tremor-dominant phenotype in the whole cohort, carriers and non-carriers did not differ on these measures of severity.
quotes: Carriers and non-carriers had similar AAO (range: 13–50 years), disease duration, age at examination, UPDRS-III and MMSE scores.

However, although G2019S carriers were more likely than non-carriers to have the PIGD motor phenotype, carriers and non-carriers were indistinguishable in terms each of these measures of clinical course.

relevance_reason: GWAS in Japanese population showing association of common variants at LRRK2 (PARK8 gene) with typical Parkinson disease susceptibility.

findings.statement: In a genome-wide association study and two replication studies involving a total of 2,011 PD cases and 18,381 controls from Japan, Satake et al. (2009) detected strong association of Parkinson disease with variants at LRRK2 on 12q12 (P = 2.72 x 10(-8)), as well as at SNCA on 4q22 (P = 7.35 x 10(-17)), both loci implicated in autosomal dominant parkinsonism. Comparison with a GWAS of individuals of European ancestry identified LRRK2 as a risk locus shared between populations; the authors concluded that autosomal dominant parkinsonism loci are involved in typical PD.
quotes: we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) and two replication studies in a total of 2,011 cases and 18,381 controls from Japan
We also detected strong associations at SNCA on 4q22 (P = 7.35 x 10(-17)) and LRRK2 on 12q12 (P = 2.72 x 10(-8)), both of which are implicated in autosomal dominant forms of parkinsonism.
we identified PARK16, SNCA and LRRK2 as shared risk loci for PD

findings.statement: Satake et al. (2009) identified PARK16 on 1q32 and BST1 on 4p15 as new PD susceptibility loci in a Japanese GWAS, and found BST1 and MAPT to show population differences compared with a European GWAS, suggesting that population differences contribute to genetic heterogeneity in PD.
quotes: We identified a new susceptibility locus on 1q32 (P = 1.52 x 10(-12)) and designated this as PARK16, and we also identified BST1 on 4p15 as a second new risk locus (P = 3.94 x 10(-9)).
BST1 and MAPT as loci showing population differences
suggest that population differences contribute to genetic heterogeneity in PD

relevance_reason: Genotype-phenotype study comparing initial PD symptoms in LRRK2 G2019S carriers versus GBA carriers and non-carriers in an Ashkenazi cohort.

findings.statement: Gan-Or et al. (2010) screened 600 Ashkenazi Jewish patients with Parkinson disease for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation and 8 GBA mutations. They compared the initial symptoms the patients reported across 3 groups: GBA mutation carriers, LRRK2 G2019S carriers, and non-carriers. More LRRK2 G2019S carriers reported muscle stiffness (rigidity, p = 0.007) and balance disturbances (p = 0.008) as initial symptoms. More GBA mutation carriers reported slowness (bradykinesia, p = 0.021). The authors suggested that LRRK2 and GBA mutations have distinct effects on the initial presentation of PD.
quotes: An extended cohort of 600 Ashkenazi PD patients was screened for the LRRK2 G2019S and for eight GBA mutations.
More LRRK2 G2019S carriers reported muscle stiffness (rigidity, p = 0.007) and balance disturbances (p = 0.008), while more GBA mutation carriers reported slowness (bradykinesia, p = 0.021).
These results suggest distinct effects of LRRK2 or GBA mutations on the initial symptoms of PD.

relevance_reason: Mutation screening of the full LRRK2 gene in 226 autosomal dominant PD families, with frequencies of G2019S and other variants in French and North African probands.

findings.statement: Lesage et al. (2009) sequenced all 51 coding exons of LRRK2 in index cases from 226 Parkinson disease families compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance, mostly from France (182) and North Africa (14). They found 79 sequence variants, 29 of them novel. Eight potentially or proven pathogenic mutations were found in 22 probands (9.7%), and most were located in the functional domains of the LRRK2 protein. The authors concluded that LRRK2 mutations are a common cause of autosomal dominant PD in Europe and North Africa.
quotes: We performed extensive mutation analyses of all 51 coding exons of the LRRK2 gene in index cases from 226 Parkinson's disease families compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance, mostly from France (n = 182) and North Africa (n = 14).
Eight potentially or proven pathogenic mutations were found in 22 probands (9.7%).
This study leads us to conclude that LRRK2 mutations are a common cause of autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease in Europe and North Africa.

findings.statement: Lesage et al. (2009) identified the common LRRK2 G2019S mutation in 13 of 226 probands (5.8%) with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease. Six of these probands were from North Africa, which was 43% of the North African probands.
quotes: The common p.G2019S mutation was identified in 13 probands (5.8%) including six from North Africa (43%).

findings.statement: Lesage et al. (2009) found 4 novel LRRK2 amino acid substitutions that they considered potentially pathogenic (S52F, N363S, I810V, and R1325Q) in probands with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease. They also found 2 novel variants, H1216R and T1410M, that they considered probably not causative.
quotes: There were four novel amino acid substitutions that are potentially pathogenic (p.S52F, p.N363S, p.I810V, p.R1325Q) and two novel variants, p.H1216R and p.T1410M, that are probably not causative.

findings.statement: Lesage et al. (2009) found the known heterozygous LRRK2 mutations R1441H and I1371V in 2 probands each with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease. They found the E334K variant in a single patient.
quotes: The known heterozygous p.R1441H and p.I1371V mutations were found in two probands each, and the p.E334K variant was identified in one single patient.

relevance_reason: Longitudinal multitracer PET study of presymptomatic members of the LRRK2 R1441C family D kindred showing that dopaminergic dysfunction progresses before clinical disease.

findings.statement: Nandhagopal et al. (2008) performed multitracer PET of presynaptic dopaminergic integrity in 13 members of family D (Western Nebraska), a parkinsonian kindred carrying the LRRK2 R1441C mutation. Five subjects were rescanned 2 to 3 years later. In 2 mutation carriers and 1 genealogically at-risk subject, PET markers declined significantly faster than the expected rate in healthy controls. The authors concluded that presymptomatic members of the kindred had dopaminergic dysfunction that progressed over time.
quotes: Thirteen family D subjects underwent PET scans of presynaptic dopaminergic integrity and five subjects were rescanned 2 to 3 years later.

In subjects 8, 9 (mutation carriers), and 13 (genealogically at risk subject), there was a decline in PET markers over the course of the study that was significantly greater than the expected rate of decline in healthy controls.
PET study of presymptomatic members of our LRRK2 kindred revealed dopaminergic dysfunction that progressed over time.

phenotypes.text: progressive presynaptic dopaminergic dysfunction on PET

findings.statement: In the LRRK2 R1441C family D, Nandhagopal et al. (2008) found that reduced dopamine transporter binding was the earliest sign of subclinical dopaminergic dysfunction. Progression to clinical disease was generally associated with the emergence of abnormal fluorodopa uptake.
quotes: Reduced dopamine transporter binding was the earliest indication of subclinical dopaminergic dysfunction and progression to clinical disease was generally associated with the emergence of abnormal fluorodopa uptake.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It shows the paper looks at whether the LRRK2 G2019S mutation is related to dyskinesias in North African patients with Parkinson disease, which bears on PARK8 genotype-phenotype correlation. No results are available.

findings.statement: Lesage et al. (2008) asked whether the common LRRK2 G2019S mutation is related to dyskinesias in North African patients with Parkinson disease.
quotes: Is the common LRRK2 G2019S mutation related to dyskinesias in North African Parkinson disease?

relevance_reason: Characterizes olfactory function and rhinencephalon alpha-synuclein pathology in LRRK2 G2019S carriers (PARK8).

findings.statement: Silveira-Moriyama et al. (2008) used the University of Pennsylvania Smell Test (UPSIT) to evaluate olfaction in 19 parkinsonian and 2 asymptomatic carriers of the LRRK2 G2019S mutation. The mean UPSIT score in parkinsonian carriers was lower than in healthy controls (p less than 0.001) and similar to that of patients with Parkinson disease (p greater than 0.999), whereas the 2 asymptomatic carriers had smell test results in the normal range.
quotes: The University of Pennsylvania Smell Test (UPSIT) was used to evaluate the sense of smell in 19 parkinsonian and two asymptomatic carriers of the G2019S mutation and compared with groups of patients with PD and healthy controls.

The mean UPSIT score in G2019S parkinsonian carriers was lower than that in healthy controls (p < 0.001) and similar to that found in patients with PD (p > 0.999). Smell tests in two asymptomatic carriers of the G2019S mutation were in the normal range.

findings.statement: Silveira-Moriyama et al. (2008) performed postmortem examination of the rhinencephalon in 4 parkinsonian carriers of the LRRK2 G2019S mutation, including 1 patient clinically found to have hyposmia, and found alpha-synuclein deposition with Lewy bodies in the olfactory pathways in all cases.
quotes: Postmortem studies of the olfactory pathways in one of the patients who had been clinically tested, and found to have hyposmia, and three other cases with the G2019S mutation, revealed alpha-syn deposition in the olfactory pathways in all cases.
We found alpha-syn accumulation with Lewy bodies in the rhinencephalon in all four cases examined pathologically.

phenotypes.text: alpha-synuclein accumulation with Lewy bodies in rhinencephalon

relevance_reason: Korean early-onset PD cohort screened for PARK genes including LRRK2; reports frequency of the LRRK2 G2385R risk variant and absence of G2019S. This is supporting evidence for PARK8 susceptibility in Asian populations.

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2008) sequenced SNCA, PARKIN, DJ-1, PINK1, and LRRK2 and analyzed gene dosage by MLPA in 72 unrelated Korean patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (onset at or before age 50) from ten movement disorder clinics in South Korea. Nine patients (12.5%) were heterozygous for the LRRK2 G2385R variant, a known Asian susceptibility allele, and none carried the G2019S mutation.
quotes: Nine patients (12.5%) had heterozygous G2385R polymorphism of LRRK2, whereas none had G2019S mutation.
The authors sequenced 35 exons in SNCA, PARKIN, DJ-1, PINK1, and LRRK2 in 72 unrelated EOPD (age-at-onset <or=50) recruited from ten movement disorders clinics in South Korea.

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2008) found that the LRRK2 G2019S mutation was absent among 72 Korean early-onset PD patients, whereas the G2385R risk variant was present heterozygously in 12.5%. Overall, variants in PARKIN, PINK1, LRRK2, and SNCA accounted for causes or genetic risk factors in 25% of Korean early-onset PD, with PARKIN mutations the most common genetic cause.
quotes: Nine patients (12.5%) had heterozygous G2385R polymorphism of LRRK2, whereas none had G2019S mutation.
We identified genetic variants in PARKIN, PINK1, LRRK2, and SNCA as a cause or genetic risk factors for PD in 25% of Korean EOPD, and mutation of PARKIN was the most common genetic cause.

relevance_reason: Transgenic Drosophila model expressing wildtype or G2019S human LRRK2 that reproduces parkinsonism-like features; animal model evidence for PARK8.

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2008) used the GAL4/UAS system to make transgenic Drosophila expressing either wildtype human LRRK2 or LRRK2 G2019S, the most common PD-associated mutation. Expressing either form in photoreceptor cells caused retinal degeneration. Expressing either form in neurons caused adult-onset selective loss of dopaminergic neurons, locomotor dysfunction, and early death. G2019S-LRRK2 caused a more severe parkinsonism-like phenotype than equivalent levels of wildtype LRRK2.
quotes: Expression of either wild-type human LRRK2 or LRRK2-G2019S in the photoreceptor cells caused retinal degeneration.
Expression of LRRK2 or LRRK2-G2019S in neurons produced adult-onset selective loss of dopaminergic neurons, locomotor dysfunction, and early mortality.
Expression of mutant G2019S-LRRK2 caused a more severe parkinsonism-like phenotype than expression of equivalent levels of wild-type LRRK2.

findings.statement: In the Drosophila model of Liu et al. (2008), L-DOPA treatment improved the locomotor impairment caused by mutant LRRK2 but did not prevent loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons. The authors described this as, to their knowledge, the first in vivo gain-of-function model that recapitulates several key features of LRRK2-linked human parkinsonism.
quotes: Treatment with l-DOPA improved mutant LRRK2-induced locomotor impairment but did not prevent the loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons.
To our knowledge, this is the first in vivo"gain-of-function" model which recapitulates several key features of LRRK2-linked human parkinsonism.

relevance_reason: This study screened Jewish Israeli patients with Parkinson disease for LRRK2 mutations. It reports how often G2019S occurs in patients and controls, a shared haplotype that points to a founder effect, and a sex effect among carriers.

findings.statement: Orr-Urtreger et al. (2007) screened Jewish Israeli patients with Parkinson disease for the LRRK2 G2019S, I2012T, I2020T, and R1441G/C/H mutations. Only G2019S was found. It was present in 14.8% of Ashkenazi and 2.7% of non-Ashkenazi patients, and in 26% of Ashkenazi familial cases and 10.6% of Ashkenazi apparently sporadic cases. Carrier frequencies in Ashkenazi and non-Ashkenazi controls were 2.4% and 0.4%, respectively.
quotes: Only the G2019S mutation was identified among our patients with PD, 14.8% in the Ashkenazi and 2.7% in the non-Ashkenazi patients, and in 26% and 10.6% of the Ashkenazi familial and apparently sporadic cases.
The carrier frequencies in the Ashkenazi and non-Ashkenazi control samples were 2.4% and 0.4%.
findings.population: Ashkenazi Jewish and non-Ashkenazi Jewish, Israel

findings.statement: Orr-Urtreger et al. (2007) used 6 microsatellite markers spanning the LRRK2 gene to determine haplotypes in 76 G2019S carriers and 50 Ashkenazi noncarrier patients with Parkinson disease. A common shared haplotype was found in all non-Ashkenazi and half-Ashkenazi carriers, and in all full-Ashkenazi carriers tested except two.
quotes: determined the LRRK2 haplotypes in 76 G2019S-carriers detected and in 50 noncarrier Ashkenazi patients, using six microsatellite markers that span the entire gene
A common shared haplotype was detected in all non-Ashkenazi and half-Ashkenazi carriers and in all full-Ashkenazi carriers tested, except two.

findings.statement: Orr-Urtreger et al. (2007) found that women and patients with a positive family history of Parkinson disease were significantly overrepresented among LRRK2 G2019S carriers. Age at onset was similar in carriers and noncarriers. The authors concluded that sex affects the frequency of the mutation among patients.
quotes: Women and patients with a positive family history of PD were significantly over-represented among the G2019S mutation carriers. Age at disease onset was similar in carriers and noncarriers.
gender affects its frequency among patients

relevance_reason: The paper screened 434 people with neurodegenerative disease for LRRK2 mutations. It found that LRRK2 mutation carriers can present with corticobasal syndrome or primary progressive aphasia, which widens the clinical range of PARK8.

findings.statement: Chen-Plotkin et al. (2008) screened 434 individuals for the common LRRK2 G2019S mutation and several other previously reported LRRK2 mutations. The group was made up of 254 patients from neurodegenerative disease clinics and 180 neurodegenerative disease autopsy cases from the University of Pennsylvania brain bank. Eight cases carried a LRRK2 mutation.
quotes: We screened for the common G2019S mutation and several additional previously reported LRRK2 mutations in 434 individuals.
A total of 254 patients recruited from neurodegenerative disease clinics and 180 neurodegenerative disease autopsy cases from the University of Pennsylvania brain bank were evaluated.
Eight cases were found to harbor a LRRK2 mutation.

findings.statement: Chen-Plotkin et al. (2008) found that 2 of the 8 LRRK2 mutation carriers first showed cognitive deficits and were clinically diagnosed with corticobasal syndrome and primary progressive aphasia, respectively. The authors concluded that LRRK2-associated neurodegenerative disease may be more clinically varied than previously assumed.
quotes: Among patients with a mutation, two presented with cognitive deficits leading to clinical diagnoses of corticobasal syndrome and primary progressive aphasia.
The clinical presentation of LRRK2-associated neurodegenerative disease may be more heterogeneous than previously assumed.

relevance_reason: Reports a family with LRRK2 G2019S-associated parkinsonism in which the proband had tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology rather than Lewy bodies, adding to the pathologic range seen in PARK8.

findings.statement: Rajput et al. (2006) described a family (Family SK) with slowly progressive parkinsonism. The affected proband had tau-immunopositive neurofibrillary tangle pathology, not the alpha-synuclein-immunopositive Lewy body pathology mainly linked to LRRK2 G2019S.
quotes: We have identified Family SK where Lrrk2 G2019S segregates with slowly progressive parkinsonism and the affected proband has tau-immunopositive neurofibrillary tangle pathology.
Lrrk2 G2019S is predominantly associated with alpha-synuclein-immunopositive Lewy body pathology.

findings.statement: In Family SK, Rajput et al. (2006) found that the LRRK2 G2019S variant segregated with slowly progressive parkinsonism. The authors suggested that alpha-synucleinopathy and tauopathy may be alternate outcomes of the same underlying genetic cause.
quotes: We have identified Family SK where Lrrk2 G2019S segregates with slowly progressive parkinsonism
Thus alpha-synucleinopathy and tauopathy, the predominant pathologies associated with parkinsonism, may be alternate outcomes of the same underlying genetic cause.

findings.statement: Rajput et al. (2006) found no evidence that either tau or alpha-synuclein protein interacts directly with LRRK2.
quotes: Intriguingly, we observe no evidence of a direct interaction between either the tau or alpha-synuclein protein with Lrrk2.

relevance_reason: Reports the clinical features of PD patients who are homozygous for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation (PARK8) and compares them with heterozygous patients.

findings.statement: Ishihara et al. (2006) described 29 patients with familial Parkinson disease who were homozygous for the LRRK2 6055G>A (G2019S) mutation. The patients came from an international consortium and included 23 Tunisians, 2 Algerians, 2 US patients, 1 Canadian, and 1 Moroccan. The authors saw no observable differences between the homozygous phenotype and previously published descriptions of heterozygous patients. They concluded that LRRK2-related PD has typical clinical features and that these similarities do not support a gene dosage effect.
quotes: Patients with familial PD and homozygous LRRK2 mutations included 23 Tunisians, 2 Algerians, 2 US patients, 1 Canadian, and 1 Moroccan.
There were no observable differences between the homozygote and heterozygote phenotypes.
Parkinson disease related to LRRK2 is characterized by typical clinical features, and the similarities between patients with homozygous and heterozygous mutations do not support a gene dosage effect.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It reports that LRRK2, the PARK8 gene product, is a component of Lewy bodies, which is relevant to how the disease develops.

findings.statement: Zhu et al. (2006) reported that LRRK2 protein is a component of Lewy bodies.
quotes: LRRK2 protein is a component of Lewy bodies.

relevance_reason: Reports neuropathology of 3 autopsied patients with the LRRK2 G2019S mutation and biochemical characterization of Lrrk2 protein; adds pathological evidence for PARK8.

findings.statement: Giasson et al. (2006) identified 3 autopsied patients with the LRRK2 G2019S mutation. Two had classic Parkinson disease with Lewy bodies, one of whom also had concurrent pathologic changes consistent with Alzheimer disease. The third had parkinsonism without Lewy bodies but showed dystrophic neurites in the substantia nigra intensely stained for Lrrk2; such Lrrk2 accumulations were unique to this patient.
quotes: Three patients with the G2019S Lrrk2 mutation were identified. Two patients demonstrated classic PD with Lewy bodies, although concurrent pathological changes consistent with Alzheimer's disease were also present in one of these individuals.

The third patient was characterized by parkinsonism without Lewy bodies but demonstrated dystrophic neurites in the substantia nigra intensely stained for Lrrk2. Lrrk2 accumulations were unique to this patient

findings.statement: Using a Lrrk2-specific antibody, Giasson et al. (2006) found that Lrrk2 was not detected in other types of pathologic inclusions, and that Lrrk2 is predominantly a soluble approximately 250-kD cytoplasmic protein expressed throughout the brain and in many other organs. They suggested that LRRK2 mutations may prime select neuronal populations to cellular insults that can lead to aberrant protein aggregation.
quotes: Lrrk2 was not detected in other types of pathological inclusions. Biochemical analysis showed that Lrrk2 is predominantly a soluble approximately 250 kDa cytoplasmic protein expressed throughout the brain but also in many other organs.
Lrrk2 mutations may prime select neuronal populations to cellular insults that can lead to aberrant protein aggregation.

relevance_reason: Reports the frequency of LRRK2 G2019S in a Parkinson disease/Lewy body disease autopsy series and finds that Lewy body disease is the most common neuropathology in carriers. It also finds the variant in a control and an Alzheimer patient, which the authors attribute to reduced penetrance.

findings.statement: Ross et al. (2006) found the LRRK2 G2019S substitution in about 2% (8) of 405 Parkinson disease/Lewy body disease cases. They also found it in 1 control subject and 1 patient with Alzheimer disease, and attributed this to reduced penetrance.
quotes: Lrrk2 G2019S was observed in approximately 2% (n = 8) of our Parkinson's disease/Lewy body disease cases (n = 405).
The mutation was also found in one control subject and one Alzheimer's disease patient, reflecting reduced penetrance.

findings.statement: Ross et al. (2006) reported that Lewy body disease was the most common neuropathology in Parkinson disease associated with LRRK2 G2019S.
quotes: Herein, we report that the most common neuropathology of G2019S-associated Parkinson's disease is Lewy body disease.

relevance_reason: The paper is a case-control association study. It reports that common LRRK2 variation, including a risk haplotype, is associated with sporadic Parkinson disease in a Chinese population.

findings.statement: Skipper et al. (2005) used tagging SNPs to evaluate common genetic variation across LRRK2 in a large, epidemiologically matched case-control series of 932 Chinese individuals with sporadic Parkinson disease or controls. Both single-tSNP and haplotype analyses gave significant evidence of disease association. Carrying 2 copies of one haplotype sharply increased disease risk (OR = 5.5, 95% CI 2.1-14.0, P = 0.0001). The authors concluded that common variation within LRRK2 contributes to the risk of sporadic Parkinson disease in the Chinese population.
quotes: Both single tSNP and tSNP haplotype analyses, using a large epidemiologically matched sporadic case-control series comprising 932 individuals, yielded significant evidence for disease association.
We identified a haplotype that dramatically increases disease risk when present in two copies (OR=5.5, 95%CI=2.1-14.0, P=0.0001).
Thus, we provide the first evidence that common genetic variation within LRRK2 contributes to the risk of sporadic PD in the Chinese population.

relevance_reason: Population screening of LRRK2 mutations in idiopathic PD probands and siblings; estimates frequency of PARK8-causing mutations.

findings.statement: Farrer et al. (2005) screened 786 Parkinson disease probands, 32 affected siblings, 1,044 unaffected siblings, and 278 unrelated controls for 9 LRRK2 mutations using allelic discrimination assays. Mutations were identified in 6 probands with PD, 1 affected sibling, 1 unaffected sibling, and 1 unrelated control. The authors concluded that LRRK2 mutations only rarely cause idiopathic PD.
quotes: the authors studied 786 PD probands, 32 affected siblings, 1,044 unaffected siblings, and 278 unrelated controls
The authors designed allelic discrimination assays for nine LRRK2 mutations and identified these in six probands with PD, one affected sibling, one unaffected sibling, and one unrelated control
Thus LRRK2 mutations only rarely cause idiopathic PD.

relevance_reason: The paper reports LRRK2 mutations (G2019S and a novel I1371V) in families with autosomal dominant PD, shows segregation, and includes a case-control association study.

findings.statement: Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2005) sequenced all 51 LRRK2 coding exons in 23 probands from families with dominantly inherited Parkinson disease and found heterozygous LRRK2 mutations in 3 of them. Two probands carried the known G2019S substitution. Mutation frequencies were checked in 180 neurologically normal controls. In a large family, G2019S segregated completely with PD.
quotes: All 51 LRRK2 coding exons were sequenced in 23 probands and the mutation frequencies were evaluated in 180 neurologically normal control subjects.
The authors identified three probands with heterozygous LRRK2 mutations: two of them have the known G2019S substitution and one proband has a novel I1371V substitution.
Mutation analysis of a large family demonstrated complete segregation of the G2019S with PD.

findings.statement: Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2005) found a novel heterozygous I1371V substitution in LRRK2 in 1 of 23 probands from families with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease.
quotes: The authors identified three probands with heterozygous LRRK2 mutations: two of them have the known G2019S substitution and one proband has a novel I1371V substitution.

findings.statement: Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2005) reported that the disease in the 3 families with LRRK2 mutations had a phenotype indistinguishable from typical Parkinson disease. Age at onset was very variable in all 3 families, and APOE genotypes did not explain this variation.
quotes: The disease in the families reported here presents a phenotype indistinguishable from typical PD.
All three families demonstrate a very variable age at onset that is not explained by APOE genotypes.

findings.statement: In a case-control study, Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2005) genotyped 4 coding LRRK2 polymorphisms in 121 patients with PD and 250 normal controls, mostly white Canadians. In the patient group, 84% had onset before age 50 and 42% had a positive family history. None of the polymorphisms was associated with PD at the allelic or genotypic level (p > 0.17). Neither these genotypes nor APOE genotypes modified age at onset (p > 0.20).
quotes: For the association study the authors genotyped four coding LRRK2 polymorphisms in 250 normal control subjects and 121 patients with PD (predominantly white patients of Canadian origin), 84% of whom had age at onset before 50 years and 42% had a positive family history.
However, there was no association between PD and any of the four polymorphisms at the allelic or genotypic levels (p > 0.17).
Furthermore, the authors did not detect a modifying effect for any genotype or of APOE genotypes upon the age at onset in the PD group (p > 0.20).

relevance_reason: Haplotype analysis of the LRRK2 G2019S mutation in families with Parkinson disease, showing a common founder. This is population-genetics evidence for PARK8. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Lesage et al. (2005) performed LRRK2 haplotype analyses in European and North African families with Parkinson disease. They concluded that the G2019S mutation arose from a common founder dating from the 13th century.
quotes: LRRK2 haplotype analyses in European and North African families with Parkinson disease: a common founder for the G2019S mutation dating from the 13th century.

relevance_reason: The paper identifies an LRRK2 kinase-domain missense mutation in the original Japanese Sagamihara family that defined the PARK8 locus.

findings.statement: Funayama et al. (2005) found a missense mutation in the kinase domain of the LRRK2 gene in affected members of the Japanese Sagamihara family with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease. This family was the basis for the original definition of the PARK8 locus.
quotes: We detected a missense mutation in the kinase domain of the LRRK2 gene in members with autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease of the Japanese family (the Sagamihara family) who served as the basis for the original defining of the PARK8 Parkinson's disease locus.

variants.as_reported: missense mutation in the kinase domain

findings.statement: Funayama et al. (2005) noted that the pathology in the Sagamihara family was distinctive, with pure nigral degeneration and no Lewy bodies.
quotes: the unique pathological features characterized by pure nigral degeneration without Lewy bodies

findings.statement: Funayama et al. (2005) did not find the Sagamihara family mutation, or other known LRRK2 mutations, in Japanese patients with sporadic Parkinson disease.
quotes: We did not detect this mutation or other known mutations of the LRRK2 gene in Japanese patients with sporadic Parkinson's disease.

relevance_reason: Reports linkage of autosomal dominant Parkinson disease in four Basque families to the PARK8 locus and describes their clinical features.

findings.statement: Paisàn-Ruìz et al. (2005) genetically characterized four Basque families with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease and found evidence for linkage to the PARK8 locus, with a maximum 2-point lod score of 3.21 (theta = 0.00) at marker D12S345.
quotes: We genetically characterized four Basque families and found evidence for linkage of autosomal dominant PD to the PARK8 locus, with a maximum 2-point logarithm of odds score of 3.21 (theta = 0.00) for marker D12S345.

findings.statement: Paisàn-Ruìz et al. (2005) reported that affected members of four Basque families with PARK8-linked autosomal dominant Parkinson disease had the clinical features of typical PD, including rigidity, akinesia, and a good response to levodopa therapy. Mean age at disease onset was 55 years.
quotes: The clinical features of these families are those of typical PD, including good response to levodopa therapy, rigidity, and akinesia, and a mean age of 55 years at disease onset.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication

relevance_reason: Reports the frequency of the LRRK2 G2019S mutation in idiopathic/sporadic Parkinson disease, directly relevant to PARK8.

findings.statement: Gilks et al. (2005) directly sequenced exon 41 of the LRRK2 gene in 482 patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease, 263 of whom had pathologically confirmed disease. They found the heterozygous 2877510G-A mutation, which causes a gly2019-to-ser (G2019S) substitution, in 8 (1.6%) of the patients. The authors concluded that a common single Mendelian mutation is implicated in sporadic Parkinson disease.
quotes: We investigated the frequency of a common heterozygous mutation, 2877510 g-->A, which produces a glycine to serine aminoacid substitution at codon 2019 (Gly2019 ser), in idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

We assessed 482 patients with the disorder, of whom 263 had pathologically confirmed disease, by direct sequencing for mutations in exon 41 of LRRK2. The mutation was present in eight (1.6%) patients.
We have shown that a common single Mendelian mutation is implicated in sporadic Parkinson's disease.

findings.statement: Gilks et al. (2005) suggested that testing for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation will be important in the management and genetic counseling of patients with Parkinson disease.
quotes: We suggest that testing for this mutation will be important in the management and genetic counselling of patients with Parkinson's disease.

relevance_reason: This paper reports the LRRK2 Gly2019Ser mutation in families with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease, which directly bears on PARK8.

findings.statement: Di Fonzo et al. (2005) sequenced the coding region of LRRK2 in 61 unrelated families with Parkinson disease and autosomal dominant inheritance.
